covers: Symptom -> root cause -> fix history. Check here first for anything that smells like a repeat of a diagnosed issue.

entries.symptom: Signed-out visitor on prod clicking a guarded link (e.g. /profile) lands on https://localhost:3020/signin?... (dead URL)
entries.root_cause: middleware built redirect URLs from url.origin, which Next resolves from the internal bind address (127.0.0.1:3020) not the Host header
entries.fix: derive all redirect URLs from getPublicOrigin(request); applied to src/middleware.ts and the auth refresh route

entries.symptom: Any /api/* Next route handler answers with Express's 'Cannot GET /api/...' in production only (works in dev)
entries.root_cause: nginx proxies the entire /api/* prefix to the Express backend before Next ever sees the request; per-path carve-out is impossible because BFF paths intentionally mirror backend paths (e.g. /auth/otp/send exists on both)
entries.fix: moved all route handlers from src/app/api/** to src/app/bff/** (git mv); repointed every browser call site; added /bff to seo.ts privateRoutePrefixes

entries.symptom: Apple sign-in button renders on /signin but fails immediately with invalid_client
entries.root_cause: NEXT_PUBLIC_APPLE_SERVICES_ID held a Google iOS OAuth client id (…apps.googleusercontent.com, copied from GoogleService-Info.plist) instead of an Apple Services ID; the render guard only checks non-empty, not validity
entries.fix: set NEXT_PUBLIC_APPLE_SERVICES_ID=com.uplisoft.velocityesim.web in .env.local and .env.production; also required creating the Services ID in Apple Developer portal (cannot be done from code) and adding APPLE_BUNDLE_ID/APPLE_SERVICES_ID to the backend .env

entries.symptom: Google sign-in fails ONLY in production with a generic 'Access blocked: Authorisation error... doesn't comply with Google's OAuth 2.0 policy' — works fine on localhost
entries.root_cause: that message is Google's generic body text for redirect_uri_mismatch; https://esim.uplisoft.com was missing from the OAuth client's Authorized JavaScript origins. Worked locally because Google ignores the port for localhost origins (masked that localhost:3000 wasn't registered either)
entries.fix: added https://esim.uplisoft.com to Authorized JavaScript origins in Google Cloud Console — NO code change

entries.symptom: Neither Google nor Apple button appears on /signin at all
entries.root_cause: SocialSignInButtons returns null when both NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID and NEXT_PUBLIC_APPLE_SERVICES_ID are empty; repo had no env file at all
entries.fix: added .env.local with NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID copied from backend's GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID (must match or backend rejects token aud); added .env.example documenting all vars

entries.symptom: Google sign-in button visually left-aligned instead of centered/full-width
entries.root_cause: Google Identity Services renders into a fixed-pixel-width iframe; CSS utility classes on the wrapper don't affect the iframe's own rendered width
entries.fix: measure the row with ResizeObserver, pass real pixel width to renderButton() (capped at Google's 400px max), re-render on resize

entries.symptom: A local .env.local change 'works on my machine' but has no effect after deploying with update.sh
entries.root_cause: .env.local is gitignored and never exists on the server; update.sh deploys via git pull then builds, so only committed env files (.env.production) reach prod
entries.fix: n/a — this is a standing operational trap, not a one-time bug; always mirror NEXT_PUBLIC_* additions into .env.production (and .env.example) if they must reach prod

entries.symptom: The Product Hunt banner on the homepage shows an old/outdated eSim2you logo even after the brand's local logo assets were updated
entries.root_cause: ProductHuntFeature (src/app/page.tsx) hot-linked its logo image from ph-files.imgix.net (a Product-Hunt-hosted snapshot taken at launch time) instead of using a local public/*.png asset, so it never picked up later logo changes
entries.fix: Point the section at public/logo-icon.png (same mark Navbar.tsx uses) instead of the ph-files.imgix.net URL; any future logo update to that asset now propagates here automatically

entries.symptom: All destination lists on the homepage and /destinations appear empty ("ALL DESTINATIONS (0)", "No destinations match these filters"), and the Help Me Choose wizard's country search returns "No destination found" for every query, even a real country name
entries.root_cause: GET /bff/packages/groups (and /bff/packages) returned 502 because the local backend dev server (E-SIM backend, feature/package-groups-api) wasn't running while the frontend dev server was pointed at BACKEND_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4000/api -- a local dev-environment gap, not an application bug. A stale orphaned `next dev` process from an earlier session (different/unknown env at its own startup time) compounded the confusion by still answering on :3000 with the same symptom even after the backend was restarted, until it was killed and a fresh dev server was started.
entries.fix: Start the backend dev server (`cd "E-SIM backend" && pnpm dev`) before the frontend when developing locally against it, and if a request still 502s after confirming the backend answers curl http://127.0.0.1:4000/health directly, check for and kill a stale/orphaned `next dev` process on :3000 (lsof -ti:3000) rather than assuming the code is broken -- verify the frontend's own request (curl http://localhost:3000/bff/packages/groups) succeeds before debugging further. Separately, DestinationBrowse.tsx and HeroDestinationChips.tsx now surface a distinct 'couldn't load, try again' UI on a fetch failure (f073) instead of rendering the same empty-state copy a genuinely zero-result response would show, so this class of failure is visibly distinguishable from 'there really are no matches' going forward.

entries.symptom: Help Me Choose wizard's destination search (step 3) returns 'No destination found' for real country names even though the backend is confirmed healthy and GET /bff/packages/groups returns real data
entries.root_cause: DestinationBrowse.tsx's autoOpenWizard path used to seed wizardOpen straight from the prop (useState(autoOpenWizard)), opening the wizard the instant the component mounted -- on a slow connection this could render HelpMeChooseWizard with an empty `countries` array before fetchPackageOptions() had resolved, so any query in step 3 matched nothing regardless of whether the data eventually arrived fine.
entries.fix: The wizard's auto-open is now gated on two effects: a WELCOME_MIN_DELAY_MS (2000ms) timer AND `!loading`, both must be true before setWizardOpen(true) fires (f074) -- a slow fetch extends the new WizardWelcomeIntro screen instead of opening the wizard early. Also check the more mundane cause first: the local backend dev server not running (see the empty-destination-lists entry above) -- both symptoms look identical from the UI and were confused with each other while diagnosing this live.

entries.symptom: A destination page (e.g. /destinations?country=hungary) throws a next/image runtime error: "Invalid src prop ... hostname \"thumb.wikimedia.org\" is not configured under images in your next.config.js"
entries.root_cause: src/app/bff/country-image/route.ts's createImageResult() uses image?.thumburl ?? image?.url from Wikimedia's imageinfo API response -- Wikimedia serves images from more than one subdomain (upload.wikimedia.org for originals, thumb.wikimedia.org for thumbnails) depending on which field comes back for a given image, but next.config.mjs's images.remotePatterns only allowlisted the single literal hostname upload.wikimedia.org.
entries.fix: Widened the remotePattern to hostname: '*.wikimedia.org' (f076) instead of allowlisting hosts one at a time as they show up for other countries. next.config.mjs changes require a full dev-server restart to take effect, unlike component code changes -- don't assume a fix didn't work just because a hot-reloaded page still errors.

entries.symptom: Web frontend shows only the plain (already-discounted) price for a package the admin has discounted via /xpricing -- no strikethrough original price or -N% badge, even though the backend computes hasDiscount/retailPrice correctly and the mobile app shows it fine
entries.root_cause: services/packages.ts's mapPackageToOption only copied hasDiscount/retailPrice through to the frontend's HeroPackageOption when retailPrice > priceNumeric -- an extra guard added when the feature was first built for the web, that mobile's equivalent (formatRetailPriceLabel) never had. Any admin discount with discountDirection:'increase' (marks the price UP, still hasDiscount:true), or any other case where retailPrice ends up <= priceNumeric, silently dropped hasDiscount/retailPrice entirely instead of just not showing a percent-off badge.
entries.fix: Removed the magnitude guard (f078) -- mapPackageToOption now copies hasDiscount/retailPrice through whenever the backend sets hasDiscount:true and retailPrice is a number, no comparison against priceNumeric. discountPricing.ts's discountPercentOff (the '-N%' badge) independently returns null when the computed percent isn't positive, while hasActiveDiscount/formatOriginalPrice (the strikethrough original price) stay unconditional on hasDiscount alone -- mirrors mobile's formatDiscountBadge/formatRetailPriceLabel split exactly.

entries.symptom: Picking a specific country in the Help Me Choose wizard (step 3) shows every plan for that destination on /destinations?country=X, ignoring the trip-length/data-need answers the user just gave in steps 1-2
entries.root_cause: WizardResult's 'country' variant only ever carried countryCode, not days/data; DestinationBrowse.tsx's handleWizardFinish navigated with router.push(`/destinations?country=${code}`) alone, and DestinationPlans.tsx (the per-country page) never read filter query params at all -- the filters-in-URL mechanism (wizardFiltersToQueryParams/parseDestinationFiltersFromParams/matchesDestinationFilters) only worked for the country-less 'skip destination' exit into the all-destinations grid (DestinationBrowse), not the single-country page.
entries.fix: WizardResult's 'country' variant now carries days/data too; wizardFiltersToQueryParams takes a plain {days,data} so both the 'country' and 'filters' branches can call it; handleWizardFinish appends filter params alongside ?country=; page.tsx forwards the same params it already parsed for DestinationBrowse to a new DestinationPlans searchFilters prop, which applies matchesDestinationFilters ahead of the page's own local filter/sort UI (f082).

how_to_use: Grep symptom text or facts ids here before re-diagnosing an auth/routing/env issue on this app — several past incidents look like 'X is broken' but were single mis-set env values, not code bugs.
